A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same gradient-alignment and SOAP study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical experiments on ten PDE benchmarks, optimizer comparisons, gradient-alignment measurements, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains the original PDE experiments and reports additional optimizer results, including the Poisson and heat comparisons in Table 2.

M1.justification: The alignment metric, SOAP eigenspace Adam updates, network architectures, and loss-balancing and causal-training procedures are retained. Explicitly writing the weight projection and adding optimizer implementation details do not establish a changed proposed method.

E1.justification: The ten main PDE benchmarks remain unchanged. v2 Section 5 and Table 2 additionally evaluate Poisson and Heat 2D problems, a limited extension within the same neural PDE-solving domain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds Kron and Muon across the ten main benchmarks and Adam+L-BFGS on four benchmarks to v1 Table 1's Adam/SOAP comparison. Table 2 newly evaluates NGD against SOAP. In the five-PDE alignment comparison, Kron replaces LAMB (v1 Figure 2; v2 Figure 5).

E3.justification: The new NGD/SOAP comparison introduces float32 versus float64 evaluation and MLP configurations varying depth and width. The retained ten-benchmark data-generation resolutions and tabulated training configurations match between v1 Tables 3-4 and v2 Tables 5-6; newly disclosed optimizer settings do not establish changes to those experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds precision and network-size sensitivity analysis for NGD versus SOAP, including discussion of convergence failures. The gradient-alignment diagnostic results are revised, while the architecture, preconditioner-frequency, and momentum ablations in Figure 4 are unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies ten random seeds for the NGD/SOAP comparison and reports numerical ± quantities in Table 2. Their meaning is undefined, and the accompanying description of 'best results' leaves aggregation unclear. v1 already contains shaded alignment plots but gives no repeated-run count; additional runs for retained experiments are not established.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial optimizer and NGD comparison results and revises the alignment trajectories. Under the unchanged tabulated benchmark settings, SOAP's reported Grey-Scott error changes from 1.18e-4 to 1.88e-4 and Kolmogorov-flow error from 6.99e-2 to 3.20e-2. New Table 3 results place Muon ahead of SOAP on Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and Ginzburg-Landau; most original Adam/SOAP entries and runtime results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition 2 and Appendix F.2 linking alignment to one-step and two-step loss reduction. It replaces v1's Newton-specific Lemma 1 with Proposition 4 and Appendix C on general preconditioners and learning-rate constraints, and removes v1 Proposition 2 and its asymptotic intra-step SOAP-alignment proof. The initialization analysis is retained and promoted from the appendix, rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: The five central contributions, ten-benchmark performance claim, and high-Reynolds-number claim remain. v2 emphasizes quasi-second-order optimizers collectively and removes the conclusion's prominent assertion that PINNs capture fine-scale dynamics more accurately than high-resolution numerical solvers, although related spectral claims remain in the experimental section.

C2.justification: v1 uses Muon to support a limitation of Shampoo-style preconditioning; v2 instead emphasizes Muon's alignment benefits alongside SOAP and Kron. v2 adds substantive NGD precision, stability, and scalability critiques and learning-rate interpretations. It also removes the extended speculation that test-error plateaus indicate convergence toward solutions more accurate than numerical references.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix G.4 adds optimizer-specific settings, including Muon's Newton-Schulz coefficients and ten iterations, and Section 3 explicitly documents scoring transformed gradients. The abstract newly supplies a code/data access link, although the checklist still promises release upon acceptance. Most architecture, data-generation, hardware, and training details were already present.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands comparative positioning through Table 1 and discussion of SOAP, Kron, Muon, NGD, L-BFGS, and gradient-surgery methods. It adds literature on DCGD, preconditioned stochastic gradient descent, activations, embeddings, and transfer learning, while removing several general multi-task and optimizer citations. Much of the PINN application survey is relocated from v1 Appendix B, rather than newly added.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work is integrated into the introduction, the methods narrative is reorganized into separate alignment, initialization, and quasi-second-order sections, and SOAP's algorithmic exposition moves into the appendix. v2 also adds a conference checklist.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different conference layout, adds optimizer-complexity and NGD tables, and expands the main performance table. The original five-row alignment figure is revised and relocated to the appendix, with a separate Navier-Stokes display in the main text. Most other figures, including Figures 3-4 and benchmark illustrations, retain their content but are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: The broader optimizer comparisons address v1's predominantly Adam-based empirical comparison, and added implementation details improve reproducibility. However, new Equation (5.2) is inconsistent even with damped Newton on a quadratic: consecutive gradients remain parallel with alignment 1, whereas the equation predicts 1 - eta^2/2 + O(eta^3). This undermines an important theoretical addition. Together with Table 2's unclear best-of-ten versus ± reporting, these reliability problems prevent a confident net quality judgment despite the empirical gains.
